channel.title: Weekly Digest
channel.description: The week's main stories from your sources

item.title: AI leaders push for slower development amid global regulatory debate
item.description: Major AI companies and leaders are calling for a pause in AI advancement, while Trump labels opposition as a conspiracy. The U.S. and China are in conflict over AI regulation, with the UN warning of risks to human rights. Why it matters: The debate over AI regulation could shape the future of technology and global power dynamics. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Al Jazeera, Ara, BBC World, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail-in voting restrictions
item.description: The US Supreme Court ruled against Trump's efforts to limit mail-in voting ahead of midterms. The decision prevents immediate implementation of his restrictions, which could have affected millions of voters. The court did not specify the vote split among justices. Why it matters: The ruling preserves current voting access and prevents potential disenfranchisement of voters ahead of key elections. (Sources: Al Jazeera, El País, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Sánchez pledges to resolve Ceuta crisis by year-end
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has committed to restoring stability in Ceuta by the end of the year, addressing a migrant influx and diplomatic tensions with Morocco. He dismissed claims of Moroccan blackmail, calling them fake news. Why it matters: The situation in Ceuta has significant implications for Spain's migration policy and international relations. (Sources: 20minutos, El País, Nació Digital, Público, RTVE, eldiario.es)

item.title: Electoral Board Divided on Supreme Court's Vote Suspension Order
item.description: Spain's Central Electoral Board voted 7-6 to comply with the Supreme Court's order suspending voting rights for naturalized citizens under the Grandchildren's Law. The decision includes a request for verification of exiled status. The Spanish government criticized the ruling as politically motivated. Why it matters: The decision affects the voting rights of approximately 400,000 citizens and highlights tensions between the judiciary and the executive branch. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Directa, La Vanguardia, Público, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Leaders of Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland unite for self-determination
item.description: Leaders from Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland have signed a declaration supporting self-determination, asserting that Westminster cannot block democratic processes. They plan to campaign together for independence from the UK and EU membership. The meeting in Cardiff highlighted their shared goal of shaping their own futures. Why it matters: This alliance could reshape the political landscape of the UK and its relationship with the EU. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, Nació Digital, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Catalan government plans to air-condition all public schools by 2031
item.description: The Catalan government has announced a €2.5 billion plan to air-condition all public schools and 51 care homes by 2031. An initial €100 million will be allocated to upgrade 100 priority centers by 2028, with the remaining 2,430 buildings to be addressed in the next two years. Why it matters: This initiative aims to improve student comfort and health in schools while addressing climate risks. (Sources: 3Cat (324), RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb)

item.title: Israeli NGO accuses government of pursuing 'elimination' project in West Bank
item.description: An Israeli NGO claims Israeli authorities are using violence, mobility restrictions, and economic pressure to undermine Palestinian life in the West Bank. Multiple sources report a coordinated effort to erode Palestinian collective existence. Some outlets note the escalation since the 2022 formation of Netanyahu's government. Why it matters: The alleged systematic erosion of Palestinian life in the West Bank could have long-term consequences for regional stability and human rights. (Sources: Al Jazeera, El País, La Vanguardia, RTVE, eldiario.es)

item.title: Spain's democracy faces challenges amid corruption and political shifts
item.description: Spain's democracy is under pressure from corruption, while the Ceuta crisis has shifted political support. The PSOE saw a two-point drop in support, with Vox gaining the most. The left and right remain closely contested. Why it matters: The political realignment could reshape Spain's governance and policy priorities. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El Salto, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Apple TV's 'Widow's Bay' wins 14 Emmy awards, topping major categories
item.description: Apple TV's 'Widow's Bay' dominated the Emmy awards, winning 14 prizes including best comedy and best actor. 'The Pitt' retained its title as best drama. The series, a horror-comedy set in a cursed town, was a standout in its genre. Why it matters: The success of 'Widow's Bay' highlights the growing influence of streaming platforms in shaping television awards and audience preferences. (Sources: Ara, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb)

item.title: Fire at Mataró textile factory causes thick smoke column
item.description: A fire at a textile factory in Mataró caused a dense smoke column visible across the area. Over 200 workers evacuated the building themselves. Firefighters are working to extinguish the blaze, which has become complicated due to the presence of flammable materials. Why it matters: The incident highlights the risks of industrial fires and the importance of emergency response in densely populated areas. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Nació Digital)

item.title: Fourth female student killed in Morelos, authorities investigate as femicide
item.description: A 21-year-old Spanish exchange student was murdered in Morelos, Mexico. Authorities are treating the death as a femicide, with no confirmed connection to previous cases. Support is being provided to her family by local officials and the Spanish Consulate. Why it matters: The incident highlights ongoing concerns about gender-based violence in Mexico and the safety of international students. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, eldiario.es)

item.title: Oasis to Perform in Barcelona in July 2027
item.description: Oasis has confirmed two concerts in Barcelona on July 10 and 11, 2027, as part of their global tour. The event will take place at the Olympic Stadium. Ticket sales will differ from previous events due to high demand. Why it matters: The concerts represent a significant cultural event for fans in Catalonia and mark Oasis's return to Spain after 18 years. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Ara, Nació Digital, RAC1, RTVE)

item.title: Sweden's far right faces first electoral loss in decades
item.description: Sweden's legislative elections saw the far-right Sweden Democrats lose support for the first time in four decades. The center-left coalition holds a narrow lead, but the final outcome depends on overseas votes. Why it matters: The shift signals a potential realignment in Swedish politics, with the far right's influence waning despite its earlier growth. (Sources: Ara, BBC World, El País, Nació Digital, The Guardian World, VilaWeb)

item.title: Marina Vilalta, la pastora más longeva de Catalunya, falleció a los 99 años
item.description: Marina Vilalta, reconocida como la pastora en activo más longeva de Catalunya, falleció a los 99 años. Trabajó como pastora desde muy joven y vivía en el Ripollès. Recibió la Creu de Sant Jordi en 2022 por su dedicación a la ramadería y la difusión de tradiciones orales. Why it matters: Su vida refleja la importancia de las tradiciones rurales y el trabajo en la agricultura tradicional. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: French President to Visit Spain September 29-30
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will visit Spain on September 29 and 30. The state visit includes meetings with King Felipe VI and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The announcement was made jointly by Spanish and French presidential offices. Why it matters: The visit highlights diplomatic engagement between France and Spain on key bilateral issues. (Sources: 20minutos, Ara, El País, RTVE)
